RJR Interoffice Memorandum

MAR 27 1987

50811 2328

Subject: Use of KYDEX(R) For A Waste Tub Stand

To: Mr. Bill Hunt

From: Dr. Rob Harrington

Scientific Affairs has reviewed and approved the use of Kydex(R) for waste tub stand at RJRT. Kydex(R) plastic sheets (Rohm & Haas Co., Philadelphia, PA) are composed of a polyacrylic-polyvinyl chloride polymer. Below is the evaluation of Kydex(R).

Polyacrylate is a polymer composed of acrylic acid monomers. Acrylic acid is of low to moderate toxicity with an oral LD50 (lethal dose to 50% of the population) in rats and mice of 340 and 2600 mg/kg, respectively. While there is no acute toxicity data on polyacrylate, the toxicity of the polymeric form of a compound is considerably lower than that of the monomer. Pyrolysis of polyacrylate generates CO, CO₂ and acetic acid. Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) is a polymer formed by linking vinyl chloride monomers in a long chain. Vinyl chloride monomer is a gas at room temperature. It has a low index of toxicity. It has been reported to be carcinogenic in rats, mice and hamsters, and is a suspect human carcinogen. Polyvinyl chloride (a polymer), however, is a solid that has a very low order of toxicity and is not carcinogenic. Rats fed a diet of 12% PVC for 2 years did not demonstrate any adverse biological effects (Smyth et. al., Toxicol Appl. Pharm. 9: 501, 1966). In the PVC form, little or no unreacted vinyl chloride monomer is present. Pyrolysis of PVC liberates significant quantities of hydrogen chloride, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide and small amounts of a variety of organic products.

Due to the low toxicity of the Kydex(R) polymer, no adverse biological effects are expected from the use of the material at RJRT.
